newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania vows to redress wrong done to exiled King.
newsitem.headline: Romania vows to redress wrong done to exiled King.

text.p: Romania's new centrist government pledged on Wednesday to redress an injustice done to the country's exiled King Michael by former Communists who stripped him of his Romanian citizenship 48 years ago.

"The Romanian government will take urgent steps to scrap the arbitrary decision of 1948," a government statement said, reacting to royalists and leading Romanian intellectuals who had appealed to Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea to restore Michael's rights as a Romanian citizen.

Michael, now 75, was dethroned and bundled into exile in 1947 by Moscow-backed Communists who seized power in Romania after World War Two. They stripped him of his Romanian citizenship one year later.

In a break from the stand taken by previous post-communist governments on the former monarch, who lives in exile in Switzerland, the government used his former official title of "King Michael I" in Wednesday's statement.
The former ruling leftists, who were thrown out of office in presidential and general elections last November, had insisted on referring to Michael as "the ex-King".
"The Justice Ministry will present to the government a solution in order to repair the injustice done by the Communists in 1948," the statement said.
Officials from Michael's Swiss residence at Versoix had no immediate reaction.
Michael was feted by hundreds of thousands of well- wishers during an emotional Orthodox Easter homecoming in 1992.

His subsequent homecoming attempts were thwarted by ex-President Ion Iliescu's leftist supporters, who insisted that in order to be allowed to visit, he should recognise the post-communist constitution of 1991 which defines Romania as a republic.
Iliescu had painted his centrist rival Emil Constantinescu as a closet monarchist during last November's elections, in a desperate bid to maintain his seven-year grip on power.
Michael hailed the reformers' election victory over the ex-communists and pledged to defend his country's interest worldwide.
"This is not the time for interminable legal or constitutional disputes," he said in a statement issued to Romanian media after the polls three months ago.
